review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp, norm_cast and fun_prop attributes: tendsto_coe_nhds_top, tendsto_ofReal_nhds_top, ofNNReal_limsup/liminf, Metric.ediam_closure/diam_closure, and Real.ediam_Ioo/Icc/Ico/Ioc. I found no conflicting rules or rewrite cycles. The cast lemmas push casts inward, which is the right direction. The ediam interval lemmas are simp, and each of their proofs is a short simp/rw script. Mathlib uses Real.ediam_Icc through simp_rw and simp only, and ediam_closure through rw. Real.diam_Icc/Ico/Ioc/Ioo have no uses anywhere in Mathlib that I could find. The only finding is the missing simp coverage of the diam interval lemmas, which is a low-confidence suggestion. I did not look for competing simp lemmas on Metric.diam of intervals outside this file beyond a grep for the diam_* names. The Lean 4 core and Batteries roots were not needed.

findings.excerpt: theorem diam_Icc {a b : ℝ} (h : a ≤ b) : Metric.diam (Icc a b) = b - a := by
findings.problem: The `Metric.ediam` of the four real intervals is simp-normalised by `@[simp] ediam_Ioo/Icc/Ico/Ioc`, which rewrite to `ENNReal.ofReal (b - a)`. The corresponding `Metric.diam` lemmas are not simp, even though they differ only by a side condition `a ≤ b`. `Metric.diam` is a plain definition (`(ediam s).toReal`), so simp cannot reach the answer through the ediam lemmas unless it unfolds `Metric.diam`. The proofs themselves show this: each is `simp [Metric.diam, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (sub_nonneg.2 h)]`. So a goal containing `Metric.diam (Set.Icc a b)` with `h : a ≤ b` in context is left unsimplified, while the ediam form is rewritten automatically. The hypothesis `a ≤ b` is a simple side goal that `simp` can discharge from hypotheses or `le_refl`, so the lemmas are suitable simp rules. They cannot loop, because the LHS is `diam` of an interval and the RHS is a real subtraction.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the four lemmas `@[simp]`, keeping the `a ≤ b` hypothesis. The ediam analogues are unconditional, so the conditional form is the right normal form for the diam versions. This gives `diam (Icc a b) = b - a` the same canonical simp treatment as `ediam (Icc a b) = ofReal (b - a)`.
findings.benefit: Users who work with `Metric.diam` of real intervals can close such goals with `simp [h]` instead of unfolding `Metric.diam` by hand. This is the same pattern the file's own proofs use. It also makes the diam and ediam simp interfaces consistent. Any downstream cost is small, since these lemmas currently have no uses in Mathlib.
